design_detail: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover laboratory trial in 12 healthy men (a 13th withdrew after two paroxetine doses and never took MDMA). Each man attended two 3-day sessions 15 days apart: paroxetine 20 mg a day or placebo on days 1 to 3, and MDMA 100 mg by mouth on day 3, 3 hours after that day's paroxetine or placebo capsule. Both day-3 conditions contained MDMA; there was no day-3 session with paroxetine and placebo MDMA, but days 1 and 2 give paroxetine-only against placebo-only comparisons. Blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, pupil diameter, a psychomotor battery and three sets of subjective scales were recorded for up to 24 hours; plasma MDMA and its metabolite HMMA for 27 hours after MDMA.
can_establish: Whether, in 12 healthy men who are extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers and have used MDMA before, three days of paroxetine 20 mg before a single 100 mg MDMA dose lowers MDMA's physical and subjectively rated effects (blood pressure, heart rate, temperature, pupil size, 'high', liking, stimulation, sociability) and changes MDMA and HMMA concentrations (MDMA peak and exposure higher by about 16% and 22%, HMMA lower by about 49% and 39%; the printed means give 38% for the exposure).
cannot_establish: What happens in women, in people who take paroxetine or another antidepressant for weeks or months (here 3 days), in people with depression or other illness, at other MDMA doses, or after a second dose (none was given); whether the lower effects come from blocking the serotonin transporter (the authors' reading; not measured here) or from other causes; anything about rare severe reactions (12 healthy men); that people on an SSRI 'take higher doses' of MDMA or what happens to their blood levels if they do (not studied: nobody took more than one dose); the share of MDMA cleared by CYP2D6 (not estimated by this design).

sample.recruitment: Men recruited by word of mouth; consent in writing; compensated; approved by the ethics committee of the Institut Municipal d'Assistencia Sanitaria, Barcelona, and authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Health (Materials and Methods, Subjects, 1st paragraph).
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Recreational MDMA use on at least 5 occasions; excluded: more than 20 cigarettes or 30 g of alcohol a day and major psychiatric disorder by structured interview (DSM-IV); a general physical examination, laboratory tests, urinalysis and 12-lead ECG were done to confirm health; negative urine screen (opiates, cocaine, cannabis, amphetamines) before each session; all participants were extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers by dextromethorphan phenotyping.
sample.demographics: All men; mean age 24 years (19 to 34), weight 71.0 kg (56.5 to 84.0), height 177 cm; 8 current smokers and 4 non-smokers; average alcohol 12 units a week; all had used cannabis, cocaine and methamphetamine; none had abuse or dependence (DSM-IV) except nicotine, and none had had a medical or psychiatric reaction to MDMA.
sample.attrition: One of 13 men withdrew on the morning of day 3 after two paroxetine doses, with insomnia, restlessness and anxiety; MDMA was not given and he is not in the results. Twelve are analysed. The subset of 7 with paroxetine and other metabolite measurements was published elsewhere.
sample.selection_effects: Men only, young, experienced with MDMA and with normal CYP2D6 activity, able to take 3 days of paroxetine (one of 13 was not); no one with depression or on long-term treatment. The result describes men like these in a hospital laboratory.

exposure.measurement: Paroxetine (Seroxat, repackaged by the hospital pharmacy in capsules identical to placebo) and MDMA (from the Spanish Ministry of Health, in capsules) given in the laboratory; plasma MDMA and HMMA by gas chromatography with mass spectrometry (method of Pizarro et al., 2002) at 14 time points to 27 hours; urine; paroxetine and other metabolites in 7 men.
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: paroxetine 20 mg a day by mouth on days 1 to 3 (about 9 AM, fasting) or placebo; MDMA 100 mg by mouth at about noon on day 3, 3 hours after that day's paroxetine or placebo capsule so that both drugs would peak together (average time to peak 2 hours for MDMA, 5 for paroxetine).
exposure.polysubstance: No other drug was given; participants were asked to abstain from drugs of abuse during the study and were screened by urine test before each session. To limit anticipation, the men were told they would receive two types of drugs, a capsule of paroxetine or placebo and, on day 3, two capsules of different doses of MDMA or placebo.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Negative urine screen required before each session; length of abstinence not stated; overnight fast.

comparison.controls: Placebo capsules on days 1 to 3 followed by MDMA 100 mg on day 3 (the same men in the other session). Days 1 and 2 compare paroxetine alone with placebo alone. There was no day-3 session without MDMA.
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Baseline and trait measures are not reported; CYP2D6 phenotype was extensive in all, with no genotype; no measure of whether the men could tell the two conditions apart.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: All had used cannabis, cocaine and methamphetamine; none met criteria for abuse or dependence except nicotine.

outcomes.instruments: Systolic and diastolic blood pressure, heart rate and oral temperature (Dinamap), pupil diameter (Haab scale), continuous ECG; psychomotor battery (digit symbol substitution, simple reaction time, Pauli test, Maddox wing); subjective scales: 49-item Addiction Research Center Inventory short form (ARCI; five scales), the in-house VESSPA questionnaire (six scales) and 21 visual analog scales; plasma MDMA and HMMA (peak, time to peak, area under the curve to 21 hours, elimination rate, half-life).
outcomes.validity_norms: Spanish validated ARCI; VESSPA is the group's own validated questionnaire (Poudevida et al., 2003); the pharmacokinetic assay is cited to an earlier paper.
outcomes.operationalization: Change from baseline; peak (Emax, 3 to 9 hours) and 6-hour area under the curve (3 to 9 hours) of each variable analysed by one-way repeated-measures ANOVA with Tukey tests, and time courses by two-way ANOVA (condition by time); pharmacokinetics by paired Student t test (peak, area) and Wilcoxon test (time to peak).
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None across outcomes: about 45 effect measures (editors' count from the Methods), each tested on area, peak and the condition-by-time term; Table 1 lists only the variables that differed significantly.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Double-blind with identical capsules; whether the men or staff could tell the conditions apart was not assessed, and paroxetine alone raised systolic pressure on days 1 and 2 (peak difference 8 mm Hg) and caused adverse effects in the 13th man.

analysis.effect_sizes: Table 2 (n=12; mean and SD): MDMA peak 212.72 (46.74) ug/L with placebo against 246.62 (55.80) with paroxetine (+15.9%, P<0.01), area to 21 hours 2115.26 (470.26) against 2572.21 (661.68) ug x h/L (+21.6%, P<0.01), time to peak 1.50 against 1.75 h, half-life 7.88 against 8.34 h (not marked significant); HMMA peak 193.14 (77.50) against 97.88 (33.83) (-49.3%), area 1923.32 (736.35) against 1189.47 (388.78) (-38.2% from the printed means; the paper's text says 39%), half-life 9.54 against 13.10 h (all P<0.01). Effects (Results and Table 1; paroxetine against placebo, MDMA on day 3): peak systolic pressure rise lower by 12 mm Hg (Emax F=22.20, P=0.001), diastolic by 5 mm Hg (Emax F=1.75, P=0.213; area F=0.27, P=0.613; significant only in the time-by-condition test, F=3.97, P<0.001), heart rate by 14 beats/min (Emax F=7.64, P=0.018; area F=3.39, P=0.093), pupil widening 3.33 to 1.23 mm (F=70.35, P<0.001), oral temperature rise lower by 0.3 C (Emax F=5.33, P=0.041; area F=2.01, P=0.184); VAS 'high' area F=41.66 and peak F=34.16 (both P<0.001), 'liking' F=15.52 (P=0.002) and 22.98 (P=0.001), 'good effects' (P<0.001 for area and peak) and 'stimulated' (area P<0.001, peak P=0.003); ARCI morphine-benzedrine group (euphoria) peak 7.27 to 4 (F=11.98, P=0.005); VESSPA sociability 3.0 to 0.58 (P=0.023), activity 5.91 to 1.21 (P=0.007), anxiety 5.55 to 2.7 (P=0.003). No significant change in 'bad effects', 'fear', 'depression or sadness', hallucination items, sedation scales, or the perception and psychotic-symptom scales; no hallucinations or psychotic symptoms; no serious adverse events; nobody needed treatment. Days 1 and 2: no difference between paroxetine and placebo except a higher systolic pressure with paroxetine (peak difference 8 mm Hg); paroxetine alone improved some psychomotor measures (digit symbol) without subjective change.
analysis.preregistration_detail: A trial authorized by the Spanish Ministry of Health; no registry entry is mentioned.
analysis.selective_reporting: Table 1 lists only the variables with a significant difference; the 7-man subset results, hormones and immune measures are published elsewhere (Segura et al., 2005; Pacifici et al., 2004).

interpretation_gap.results_show: In 12 men, three days of paroxetine before 100 mg of MDMA lowered the rise in blood pressure (systolic by 12 mm Hg at peak), heart rate (by 14 beats/min), pupil size and temperature, and lowered ratings of 'high', liking, stimulation, euphoria-type and sociability scales, while MDMA's peak concentration was 16% higher and its exposure 22% higher, and the main metabolite HMMA 49% (peak) and 39% (exposure; 38% from the printed means) lower. Diastolic pressure was not significant by the area (P=0.613) or peak (P=0.213) test, and heart rate was significant by the peak test (P=0.018) but not the area test (P=0.093).
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract and the first paragraph of the Discussion say paroxetine was associated with a 30% increase in MDMA concentrations; Table 2 and the Results give 16% (peak) and 22% (exposure), and the Discussion's second mention of 30% cites an earlier analysis of 7 men (Segura et al., 2005). The abstract says the marked decrease in effects could lead people who use MDMA to take higher doses and so to life-threatening toxic effects, and the closing paragraph says the same of depressed people on SSRIs. Nobody took a second dose, no toxicity was measured and nobody on long-term treatment was studied. The Discussion also says the reduction in systolic pressure, diastolic pressure and heart rate was significant, whereas Table 1 gives diastolic pressure P=0.213 at peak and 0.613 for area.

timeline.event: Case series of four people who had taken fluoxetine before ecstasy: one felt less effect, three felt no change (McCann and Ricaurte; cited here and in the 2000 citalopram paper; not read)
Independent group: citalopram by infusion before MDMA lowered most psychological effects of MDMA by about 60% in 16 healthy volunteers
Another group, cited here: fluoxetine given daily for at least 5 days lowered MDMA's cardiovascular and subjective effects (Tancer and Johanson; not read)
Same group: a single MDMA dose lowers CYP2D6 activity for days, so that medicines cleared by CYP2D6 and taken after MDMA would be affected

Systematic review: duloxetine and reboxetine also lowered MDMA's effects and raised peak MDMA by 15 to 18%; bupropion raised MDMA exposure but did not lower the ratings (as summarized by the review, from trials by the Zurich group of the 2000 citalopram study)

replication.where_it_stands: Blunting of MDMA's effects by serotonin reuptake inhibitors has been found by at least two other groups with other drugs (citalopram, fluoxetine), and a rise of 14 to 18% in peak MDMA with CYP2D6-inhibiting medicines was reported for duloxetine and reboxetine in trials summarized by the 2022 review (from the same laboratory as the citalopram study). All of this is small laboratory work in healthy volunteers over a single dose or a few days; no trial has studied people who take an antidepressant for illness, women in numbers, or a second dose of MDMA after an antidepressant.

funding.funder: Fondo de Investigacion Sanitaria grants FIS 97/1198, 98/0181, 00/0777 and 01/1336; Generalitat de Catalunya grant 2001SGR00407; Area Progetto Droga, Istituto Superiore di Sanita, Rome; one author held a post-training contract from the Instituto de Salud Carlos III (Introduction footnote).
funding.declared_conflicts: None stated: the article carries no conflict-of-interest statement.
funding.affiliations_note: Authors (Farre, Abanades, O'Mathuna, Torrens, de la Torre) overlap with de la Torre et al. (2000, 2012), Farre et al. (2004) and O'Mathuna et al. (2008), so these are one group's studies, not independent replications of each other.

what_would_settle_it: A randomized, double-blind crossover in people who take an antidepressant for illness at steady state, in women as well as men and in matched healthy volunteers, with a session of antidepressant and placebo MDMA, MDMA at more than one dose, plasma MDMA and metabolites, CYP2D6 genotype, a measure of whether the blind held, and a second MDMA dose or a dose-choice task so that what people do after feeling little, and what their blood levels are then, is measured rather than assumed.

domains.note: Conditions are said to be randomly assigned; sequence generation and concealment are not described.
A washout of 15 days between sessions; paroxetine and MDMA are cleared within days.

Identical capsules and a cover story; but blinding was not assessed, paroxetine raised systolic pressure on days 1 and 2, one man left with adverse effects, and the blunted MDMA experience itself may reveal the condition.
12 of 13 analysed; the one who left after two paroxetine doses never took MDMA, so the analysed men are those who tolerated paroxetine.
Plasma levels and most physiological measures are objective; the subjective scales are self-ratings that could be influenced by partial unblinding; there is no day-3 session without MDMA.
About 45 measures with three tests each and no correction; Table 1 lists only significant variables; the headline 30% rise in MDMA is not the trial's own figure (16% and 22%).

risk_of_bias.reasoning: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover with objective pharmacokinetic outcomes and a consistent pattern across many measures, but only 12 men, no confidence intervals, many uncorrected tests, a blind that may have leaked, and a three-day pretreatment. The source can be cited for lower blood-pressure, heart-rate, pupil, temperature and subjective responses to 100 mg of MDMA after 3 days of paroxetine 20 mg in 12 healthy men, with MDMA's peak 16% and exposure 22% higher and HMMA about half as high; it cannot be cited for the 30% figure, for people on long-term treatment, for what happens with a higher or second MDMA dose, or for any harm.

key_findings.finding: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover in 12 healthy men (mean age 24; all extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers; MDMA on at least 5 previous occasions); a 13th man withdrew after two paroxetine doses (insomnia, restlessness, anxiety) and never took MDMA. Two 3-day sessions 15 days apart: paroxetine 20 mg a day or placebo on days 1 to 3, MDMA 100 mg on day 3, 3 hours after that day's capsule.
key_findings.locator: Materials and Methods > Subjects, 1st and 2nd paragraphs; Study Design, 1st and 2nd paragraphs

key_findings.finding: Days 1 and 2: no difference between paroxetine and placebo in area or peak of effects except a rise in systolic pressure with paroxetine (peak difference 8 mm Hg); paroxetine alone improved some psychomotor measures (digit symbol correct responses) and changed no subjective variable.

Physiological effects of MDMA were lowered by paroxetine: peak systolic pressure by 12 mm Hg (Emax F=22.20, P=0.001), diastolic by 5 mm Hg and heart rate by 14 beats/min, pupil widening from 3.33 to 1.23 mm (F=70.35, P<0.001), temperature rise lower by 0.3 C (P=0.041); the Discussion puts the cardiovascular reduction at about 50% and pupil about 70%. By Table 1 the diastolic area (P=0.613) and peak (P=0.213) and the heart-rate area (P=0.093) were not significant.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (p. 957); Results > Physiological Effects, 1st paragraph (p. 957); Fig. 1 (p. 958); Discussion, paragraphs on cardiovascular effects and pupil diameter (pp. 959 to 960)

key_findings.finding: Subjective effects were lowered: ARCI euphoria scale (morphine-benzedrine group) peak 7.27 to 4, amphetamine scale 5.27 to 3.67; VESSPA anxiety 5.55 to 2.7, sociability 3.0 to 0.58, activity 5.91 to 1.21; VAS 'stimulated', 'high', 'any effect', 'good effects', 'liking' (all P=0.003 or less at peak) and 'different body feeling'. No significant change in 'bad effects', 'fear', 'depression or sadness', hallucination items or sedation scales; no hallucinations or psychotic symptoms, no serious adverse events, nobody needed treatment.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (p. 957); Results > Subjective Effects (p. 957); Figs. 2 and 3 (pp. 959 to 960)

key_findings.finding: Plasma concentrations of MDMA with paroxetine against placebo (Table 2, n=12): peak 246.62 against 212.72 ug/L (+16%), area to 21 hours 2572.21 against 2115.26 ug x h/L (+22%), both P<0.01; HMMA peak 97.88 against 193.14 (-49%) and area 1189.47 against 1923.32 (-38% from the printed means; the text says 39%), half-life 13.10 against 9.54 hours (all P<0.01); MDMA half-life 8.34 against 7.88 hours.
key_findings.locator: Results > Plasma Concentrations of MDMA and HMMA (pp. 957 to 958); Table 2 (p. 961)

key_findings.finding: Discussion: the main result is a marked decrease of physiological and subjective effects 'despite a 30% increase' in MDMA plasma concentration (in the abstract: 30%; in the Discussion: 'approximately 30%' citing the 7-man analysis of Segura et al., 2005); because HMMA fell by more than MDMA rose, CYP2D6 seems to contribute less to MDMA's clearance than the 60% from in vitro work; paroxetine is read as acting at the serotonin transporter (pharmacodynamic) and on CYP2D6 (pharmacokinetic), and not fully counteracting MDMA, which points to other transmitter systems.
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Discussion, 1st to 3rd paragraphs (p. 959); paragraph on SSRIs and the serotonin transporter (p. 959 to 960)

key_findings.finding: The authors close by suggesting that the marked decrease in the positive effects people seek may lead to higher MDMA doses (with depressed people who take SSRIs as their example) and so to potentially life-threatening toxic effects; the abstract makes the same suggestion. They cite internet forums, and animal studies of neuroprotection, for the idea that SSRIs are combined with MDMA.
key_findings.locator: Abstract; Introduction, 1st and 2nd paragraphs (pp. 954 to 955); Discussion, final paragraph (pp. 961 to 962)

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract and the Discussion (first paragraph) state a 30% increase in MDMA plasma concentrations with paroxetine. The trial's own Table 2 and Results give +16% for the peak and +22% for the area to 21 hours; the Discussion's second mention (30%, and HMMA 40% lower) is attributed to an earlier analysis of 7 of these men (Segura et al., 2005).
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite 16% (peak) and 22% (exposure) for this trial; the 30% is not this trial's result.

reporting_issues.issue: The text says paroxetine decreased systolic pressure, diastolic pressure and heart rate 'significantly'; Table 1 gives diastolic pressure P=0.613 (area) and P=0.213 (peak) and heart rate P=0.093 (area), significant only for the peak (P=0.018) and in the condition-by-time term.
reporting_issues.consequence: The 5 mm Hg diastolic difference and the area of the heart-rate response are not supported by the paper's own tests; the systolic, pupil and subjective results are the solid ones.

reporting_issues.issue: Both day-3 conditions contained MDMA, so paroxetine's own effect on that day cannot be separated from its effect on MDMA's, and the paper does not say whether each change from baseline is taken from the value before the day-3 capsule or just before MDMA. Days 1 and 2 show paroxetine alone raising systolic pressure (peak difference 8 mm Hg) and improving a psychomotor measure.
reporting_issues.consequence: A higher baseline under paroxetine would, if anything, work against the finding of a lower systolic response, but day-3 effects of paroxetine alone are not measured and the baseline used is unclear.

reporting_issues.issue: About 45 effect measures were each tested on area, peak and condition by time, with no correction; Table 1 lists only the variables that differed, and several values lie close to the threshold (systolic area P=0.033, drowsiness area P=0.049, 'different surroundings' P=0.041 and 0.042).
reporting_issues.consequence: Results at P<0.001 (high, any effect, good effects, liking, stimulated, pupil, systolic peak, euphoria and amphetamine scales) are the dependable ones; the near-threshold ones may be chance.

reporting_issues.issue: A 13th volunteer left after two paroxetine doses (insomnia, restlessness, anxiety); he is described in the Methods but counted nowhere in the safety statement ('serious adverse events were not observed'), and the 12 analysed are the men who tolerated paroxetine.
reporting_issues.consequence: One of 13 men could not take 3 days of paroxetine 20 mg; the trial says nothing about the MDMA and paroxetine combination in him, since he never took MDMA.

reporting_issues.issue: The conclusion that the lower effects could lead people to take higher doses of MDMA, with life-threatening toxic effects, and the example of depressed people on SSRIs, rest on no data: nobody took a second dose, no toxic effect was measured, and no person on long-term SSRI treatment was studied; the supporting references are an internet forum and animal studies.
reporting_issues.consequence: A hypothesis, not a finding: no study has measured whether people who feel less take more or what their blood levels are if they do. The only related measurements are the higher MDMA peak and exposure in this trial and the more-than-proportional rise after higher or repeated doses in other studies.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion estimates from the larger fall in HMMA (about 40-49%) than rise in MDMA (16-30%) that CYP2D6 handles less of MDMA's clearance than the 60% reported in vitro.
reporting_issues.consequence: The design cannot estimate that share (paroxetine also lowers the formation of HMMA by other routes, and the numbers differ by analysis); do not cite it as a measurement.

reporting_issues.issue: The Methods describe the pharmacokinetic area under the curve as 0 to 27 hours (blood was drawn to 27 hours after MDMA), while Table 2 labels its area 0 to 21 hours.
reporting_issues.consequence: Minor: the printed areas (+22% with paroxetine) are quoted as 'to 21 hours', as the table labels them; the paper does not explain the difference.
